marie: Heads-up — ran a sandbox profiling sweep for KV quantization (INT8 vs FP8) on long-prefix conversational traces. Seeing memory wins but intermittent decode artifacts at >=8k prefix.
ajay: can you paste the raw numbers and the command you ran? want to repro quickly.
marie: pasted below. run command:
```
rwi-bench --model redwood/insta-13b --mode decode --prefixes prefixes/8k_samples.txt \
  --kv-quant int8 --calib-mode sample_stats --batch 4 --pin-kernel auto
```
marie: results (median of 5 runs):
```
config: KV=INT8, calib=sample_stats, batch=4
memory: base (fp16 kv) = 24.8GB -> int8 kv = 8.6GB (65% reduction)
latency: decode step p50 = 46ms -> 43ms (6.5% faster) p95 = 110ms -> 118ms (8% slower)
quality: ppl on eval_prefixes +0.7, token-regen rate +0.9% (not huge but visible)
```
marie: FP8 run for same traces:
```
config: KV=FP8, calib=none, batch=4
memory: kv = 13.6GB (45% reduction)
latency: p50 = 44ms (4% faster), p95 = 105ms (4.5% better)
quality: ppl +0.12, token-regen rate +0.12%
```
ajay: interesting — FP8 gives better tail latency and much smaller quality hit. INT8 helps more on memory but tail latency worsens. suspect quantization error accumulates for long KV chains.
dan: note that we pushed the new matmul kernel selector last Tuesday (auto -> prefer-fast-gemm). could be interacting with INT8 kernels and causing p95 regressions. can you repro with --pin-kernel=old-gemm?
marie: good call. pinned kernel run now. INT8 + pin-old-gemm:
```
memory same (~8.6GB)
latency: p50 45ms, p95 106ms
quality: token-regen +0.35%
```
marie: p95 improvement back to FP8-like numbers and quality improved too. so kernel selection + INT8 interaction looks real.
tina: for the calibration mode — you used sample_stats. did you try per-head scaling? INT8 with per-tensor scales can underfit head activations.
marie: I did sample_stats global per-tensor. per-head calib run in progress.
bench-bot: automated run complete — added per-head calibration results to the bucket (s3://rwi-sandbox/kv-quant/1790001234/)
bench-bot: per-head INT8:
```
memory: 8.6GB
latency: p50 44ms p95 108ms
quality: token-regen +0.22%
```
marie: per-head looks way better than per-tensor. still slightly worse than FP8 on tail but acceptable for many customers.
odin: curious about mixed precision in the KV itself — older entries colder can be stored as int8, recent as fp8/unquantized. we have a kv-tiered prototype. did you try it?
marie: yes, kv-tiered set to threshold=2048 tokens (older -> int8, recent -> fp8) gave:
```
memory: 11.2GB
latency: p50 44ms p95 103ms
quality: token-regen +0.08%
```
marie: this seems like a good middle ground — most tail latency returns near FP8 and memory savings still solid.
dan: great. next question: batching heuristics. are larger batches amplifying the noise? i.e., when we combine KV work across requests we might see more quant-dequant hops.
ajay: I saw that when batch >=8 p95 jumps for INT8 even with per-head calib. could be because we invoke the packing path that quantizes/dequantizes per-batch. we should avoid extra +/- quant hops.
marie: reproduced: batch=8 INT8 per-head pinned-old-gemm -> p95 140ms, token-regen +1.8%.
tina: potential mitigation: move quantization to a write-once path. when building prefix KV from same conversation, quantize only once and reuse. also try using asymmetric quant with zero-point per-head — might reduce bias.
marie: tried asymmetric per-head in the prototype: token-regen down to +0.4% and p95 improved ~6ms.
oliver: for rollout planning: propose default: FP8 KV for hosted API, INT8-per-head for dedicated if customer wants max memory reduction, and kv-tiered as opt-in advanced config. also add a runtime flag to pin kernel selector when int8 is enabled until we fix the selector interaction.
marie: agree. I'll open a short RFC with numbers and suggested defaults + a small canary rollout plan. will include commands to reproduce and the S3 bucket with artifacts.
ajay: assign me to the RFC review, will validate the canary config on dedicated infra.
marie: thanks — putting reproducer and calibration scripts here: `/infra/bench/runs/1790001234/` (links in thread). TL;DR:
- INT8 gives biggest memory win (~2.9x) but needs per-head calibration and kernel pin to avoid p95 regressions for long prefixes
- FP8 is a safer default: good memory/latency with minimal quality loss
- kv-tiered gives a pragmatic middle ground for long-lived contexts
- batching path needs change to avoid repeated quant/dequant
marie: pinging @eng-runtime for visibility :eyes:
